text:
Phases 0-4 landed; phase 5 deliberately not scheduled. docs/plans/design-hardening.md is updated with what each phase actually did and marked landed.

Result against the four findings:
  3.1 id round-trip   ColumnId('my col').value == 'my.col'  ->  ids return their input or reject it
  3.2 error fidelity  4 of 14 mistakes -> BuildFailed       ->  0 of 17 -> BuildFailed
  3.3 *Either twins   44, DataTable 19 accessors            ->  36, DataTable 4 accessors
  3.5 id boilerplate  10 hand-written copies                ->  2 definitions, 10 two-line uses

design is at 157 tests green on both JVM and JS (from 153), compileAll is warning-clean, and testAll passes across every module and both platforms.

Two departures from the epic as written, both narrowing rather than widening:
 - contrasts was retyped Option[ArgValue] -> Option[String] in phase 3, on the epic's own reasoning about basis: it keys a user-extensible registry. It was the one identifier position where ColumnId would have been a lie.
 - phase 4's ~130 -> ~30 line estimate was optimistic. The repetition went 129 -> 20; the shared scaffolding that replaced it is ~70 lines. See that bead for the arithmetic.

Phase 5 (col"..." interpolators) stays unscheduled: its condition has not changed, since direct AST construction is still confined to tests, which read fine with a local one-line ColumnId.unsafe helper.
